title: How to Create Irresistible Hooks (and blow up your content)

principles.text: Clearly define the video's topic for self-selection.
Draw the audience in by leaning on relatable scenarios.
Use a single contrasting word or phrase to 'stun' the viewer and stop their scroll.
Introduce a surprising twist that goes against the initial lean, keeping the viewer curious.
Visual hooks are significantly more powerful than spoken word hooks.
People read text faster than they can hear or visually comprehend a full scene.

formulas.name: 3-Step Hook Formula (Text Adaptation)
examples: Vegas Sphere has wild tech. But get this... Least impressive part.
3 mortgage mistakes. But it's not interest rates. It's coming from...

formulas.name: X-Y-Z Compelling Hook
formulas.template: Achieve X? Don't do Y, do Z.
examples: Go viral? Don't list hooks, learn psychology.

anti_patterns: Generic filler (e.g., '25 viral hooks' without explaining why they work)

verbatim_hooks.why: Establishes context and common ground, signaling the video's topic and benefit.
Provides immediate context and creates interest in a novel topic.

verbatim_hooks.text: The tech in the Vegas Sphere is insane.
verbatim_hooks.why: Draws the audience in with an exciting statement about the topic.
Uses a compelling fact to lean the audience in.
Simplifies a complex idea (screen size) with a relatable metaphor.
A contrasting interjection to stop the scroll and build anticipation.
The contrarian snapback, creating curiosity by challenging expectations.
A direct call to action/promise of surprising information.
Establishes context and a pain point for the target audience.
A scroll-stopping interjection that challenges a common belief.
The contrarian snapback, offering a deeper, more compelling solution.

twitch_comp_notes: For mute-first viewing, burned text hooks are paramount. They must convey the core message and create curiosity instantly.
Use 3-5 bold words on screen to establish context and lean-in points.
Employ contrasting words (e.g., 'BUT', 'YET', 'HOWEVER') as burned text to create a 'scroll stop interjection'.
The 'contrarian snapback' should be a short, surprising text phrase that re-engages the viewer.
Visual cues like movement, quick cuts, and emotional reactions from the streamer should complement the burned text hooks to enhance engagement without sound.
